notes:
Executive summary:
- Prospect: Marlin Harbor Allocations (maritime logistics platform) evaluating Redwood Dedicated for inference serving of reranking + agent chat and embeddings. Primary ask: predictable latency under bursty booking loads, clear reserved GPU plan, and SLA language for enterprise procurement.

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-11: Intro call (AE + SE) — overview of Redwood Dedicated, initial throughput questions. Fireflies id ff_20260111_intro.
- 2026-01-25: Technical deep-dive with infra and ML team (Riley + Marlin infra). Discussed baseline metrics and model choices.
- 2026-02-12: Dedicated sizing workshop (2.5h) — ran traffic samples, validated token distributions, agreed next steps for POC. Fireflies ff_20260212_marlin_sizing_call.
- 2026-02-20: Follow-up email with preliminary GPU count and cost band. Gmail thread: gmail_thread:2026-01-marlin-dedicated-eval.

Requirements / constraints (from Marlin):
- Workloads: reranking for routing/pricing (primary), customer chat assistant (secondary), nightly embeddings index refresh.
- Latency targets: p95 generation latency <300ms for reranking (single-turn, short responses), p95 <700ms for chat use-cases under steady-state. p99 failover target <1.5s with fallback to smaller model.
- Throughput profile: highly spiky due to booking windows and batch index jobs. Typical steady-state QPS: 120 qps. Daily peak windows: burst up to 1,000 qps for 30-90s, and extended elevated periods ~800 qps for 5-10 minutes during global sailings release.
- Request size: average tokens/request ~90 tokens (user + response), 95th percentile ~280 tokens for longer agent flows.
- Tokens/sec math from workshop: steady-state tokens/sec ≈ 120 * 90 = 10,800 t/s; peak tokens/sec (short bursts) ≈ 1,000 * 90 = 90,000 t/s. Embeddings refresh jobs: batch throughput targets 200k tokens/sec but scheduled off-peak windows.
- Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to commit to 12–18 month reserved capacity if unit economics are competitive.
- Security: must be deployed in VPC, KMS key management, SOC2 certificate required, audit logs retained 1 year, data residency in NA.

Model & infra preferences discussed:
- Marlin experimenting with quantized 13B variants for rerank and mid-sized 33B for chat in 8-bit/4-bit quantized runs. Preference to test Llama2-13B/Redwood-snippet-13B quantized.
- KV/prefix caching is mandatory for repeated multi-turn chat sessions. Decision: enable prefix caching for primary chat routes.

Sizing workshop outcomes (deliverables):
- Microbenchmarks run during workshop: per-GPU sustained token/sec for selected model on target instance types (A100-40GB and H100 preliminary). Results: A100-ish numbers used as baseline for compute planning (see attached spreadsheet).
- Initial recommendation: reserved pool = 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs to meet steady-state + headroom (handles ~12k t/s sustained with model mix). Burst buffer = autoscale to 10 GPUs for short peaks up to ~90k t/s using fast warmup and batching.
- Fallback route: smaller quantized model (13B) deployed as lower-cost variant for non-critical traffic and aggressive p95 SLOs.
- Suggested caching/batching config: continuous batching window 15ms for reranking routes, prefix caching TTL 10 minutes for session reuse.

SLA & procurement notes:
- Marlin legal asked for: uptime SLA 99.95% for Dedicated control plane and 99.9% for inference path, credits table, and explicit latency SLOs at p95 with measurement method and traffic profile.
- AE/SE negotiating: Redwood to provide an ops playbook for failover (model fallback, regional routing) and a monthly performance report with token-level billing breakouts.

POC plan & milestones:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): small POC using Marlin shadow traffic 10% of live peak. Validate p95 & autoscaler behavior. Deliverable: POC report + tuning doc.
- Phase 2 (3 weeks): run full dedicated sizing run in Redwood Dedicated staging cluster — measure steady and burst windows. Deliverable: final sizing spreadsheet + pricing.
- Phase 3 (ops handoff): integrate alerting and per-route dashboards into Redwood Console; run security attestation (SOC2 artifact exchange).

Open questions / blockers captured during workshop:
- Exact warmup time for large-model KV cache under live booking bursts (affects autoscale policy).
- Final SOC2 artifacts timeline — security needs to approve before procurement sign-off.
- Budget cadence: procurement preparing a 12-month commit; need firm monthly ARR numbers to finalize.

Quotes / paraphrases from Marlin attendees:
- CTO: "Booking peaks are brutal — we need predictable tail latencies otherwise SLAs to our customers break."
- Head of ML: "If Redwood can give a deterministic sizing + SLA for the reranker, we'll put the core traffic on dedicated."

Next steps (short):
- Deliver finalized sizing spreadsheet with model-specific GPU counts and cost delta (action: Riley, due 2026-03-05).
- Draft SLA language for p95 latency and credits (action: Ava, legal loop).
- Schedule SOC2 artifact transfer and vendor questionnaire (Marlin security).
